name: Potters' Quarter
hero_subtitle: Working kilns, workshops and Safi’s signature craft.

overview.title: Safi’s living craft
overview.p1: The potters’ quarter is the reason many travellers stop in Safi. On the hillside, workshops and traditional kilns still produce the ceramics that made the city famous.
overview.p2: You can watch throwing, glazing and firing when artisans are at work. Bargaining for finished pieces is normal; buy what you like without pressure.
overview.p3: Morning visits are best: more workshops open and the light is softer for photos of the kilns.

food.title: Food near the potters’ quarter
food.p1: Options are limited on the hill itself; plan a meal in town or by the port.
food.li1: Cafés and snacks closer to the medina.
food.li2: Fish restaurants at the fishing port.
food.li3: Carry water — the hill can be warm.
food.li4: Do not leave food waste near workshops.
food.li5: Ask before sitting inside a working space.
food.p2: Combine the visit with lunch in the medina afterward.

tips.title: Practical tips for the potters’ quarter

1.title: Morning is better
1.desc: More workshops are active and the heat is milder.

2.title: Ask before photos
2.desc: Many artisans allow photos; always ask first, especially of people.

3.title: Buy fairly
3.desc: Bargain politely. Pack fragile pieces carefully for travel.

q1.question: Is the potters’ quarter free?
q1.answer: Walking the area is free. Workshops may sell pieces; there is no mandatory ticket.

q2.question: Can I watch pottery being made?
q2.answer: Yes when artisans are working — mornings are most reliable.

q3.question: How do I get there?
q3.answer: Petit taxi from the centre or a walk uphill from the medina side.

q4.question: What should I buy?
q4.answer: Whatever you like: plates, bowls, tiles. Check for solid glazing if you will use them daily.

q5.question: Do I need a guide?
q5.answer: Optional. A guide can introduce specific workshops; you can also wander alone.
